answer: A tide of new identities is only trusted after each one posts a small refundable bond tinted, like pigment, to its own payment history: the bond stays locked while the agent works and is slashed if two identities ever draw on the same funding source. Honest newcomers graze the shared meadow freely once their bond clears, but an attacker wanting a thousand clones must fund a thousand separate bonds, so faking stops paying while honest work stays cheap.
